policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 26 Jan close (1x4 3.78, 3x6 3.48, 6x9 3.36, 9x12 3.34 vs WIBOR 3M 3.92) price roughly 60bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The MPC held at 4.00% on 14 Jan. Glapiński (15 Jan): a terminal rate of about 3.5% with a real rate of at least 1-1.5%, cuts in 25bp steps; he excluded neither February nor March (or even April). December data beat forecasts (22 Jan): wages +8.6% y/y (6.9% expected), industry +7.3% (2.9%), construction +4.5%; ING (22 Jan) says this lowers the odds of February, with a pause until March the base case. Erste (23 Jan): the data significantly weaken the case for an early-February cut; it expects March and May. Duda (23 Jan): both February and March cuts look likely.
policy.risk_text: Strong December wages and industry cut the odds of a February move; the March projection is the gate. A hawkish projection (fiscal impulse ~7% of GDP deficit, 8.6% wages) would lift the front end; global long-end volatility and heavy supply weigh on the 10Y asset swap.

cpi.m: Dec final (GUS, 15 Jan); Nov 2.5%; Dec core 2.7% (NBP, 16 Jan)

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 CPI 2.4% y/y (final). The March 2026 projection is due with the March MPC meeting.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP; 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; FinMin Domański (16 Jan): the 2025 central-budget deficit came in a dozen-plus billion below the PLN 288.8bn limit; the President signed the 2026 budget on 19 Jan and referred it to the Constitutional Tribunal for follow-up review (the act is in force); Eurostat (22 Jan): general-government debt 58.1% of GDP at end-Q3 2025.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions; 2026 needs ~28% financed (26 Jan); a USD 10bn SEC shelf was filed on 20 Jan (published 21 Jan); Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks; Coface (20 Jan) flagged downgrade risk if the deficit path does not improve.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% and held on 14 Jan; December CPI 2.4% y/y (final, 15 Jan), core 2.7%; the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters 2.6%); the March projection is the next policy gate. GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3; IMF (19 Jan) raised Poland's 2026 growth forecast to 3.5%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 26 Jan: December retail sales +5.3% y/y (5.6% expected); M3 +10.4%; MoF: 2026 needs ~28% financed; 28 Jan offer published. Abroad: gold above $5,000, the dollar index at 96.97 (-2% in six sessions), Ifo 87.6; markets see the next Fed cut in June.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance; January sales 9 Jan (done: PLN 13.7bn incl. additional sale), 22 Jan (plan 8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); EUR 3.25bn priced on 8 Jan. 16 Jan: 36-week T-bills PLN 3.8bn at 3.645%. MoF filed a USD 10bn shelf prospectus with the US SEC (20 Jan). 22 Jan result: PLN 12.0bn sold vs 17.1bn demand (cover 1.43) plus 1.75bn additional (NZ0331 1.04bn, WZ0930 0.59bn); stop yields OK0128 3.488%, PS0131 4.386%, DS0432 4.611%, DS1035 5.107%. MoF (26 Jan): ~28% of 2026 needs financed. 28 Jan offer (MoF, 26 Jan): PLN 8-12bn in OK0128, WZ0930, PS0131, NZ0331, DS1034 (re-opened) and DS1035.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (28 Jan) rather than the day before. January auctions have been absorbed with cover of 1.4-1.9x, so supply is not the binding constraint. For the front end the 3-4 Feb MPC is the next event: strong December data pushed the consensus to a February hold; the March projection decides the cut timing.

core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~60bp more priced, the ECB is done at 2.00% (a hike is the next move in market pricing), the Fed is on hold into June, the BoE eases gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 57bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 226bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 26 Jan close). Dollar index 96.97 (-2% in six sessions) and gold above $5,000 (26 Jan).
